provenance.note: Generated by drivers/survival on the pystatsval harness against a PyPI-installed pystatistics==5.0.0 (confirmed: installed in site-packages via pip, dist-info present; the standalone detect_install_source() helper was removed from the library in 5.0.0). 5.0.0 is a RENAME-ONLY release over the blessed 4.8.0 line: the statistical engine is byte-for-byte unchanged and only public API symbols were renamed library-wide (GammaFamily -> Gamma with no alias, the 'negative.binomial' family string -> 'negative-binomial', and the regression ridge keyword lam= -> l2=). The survival module's public surface uses NONE of the renamed symbols: kaplan_meier / survdiff / coxph / discrete_time take positional args, the KM solution's .ci_lower/.ci_upper and the Cox/discrete .standard_errors accessors were already at their current names at 4.8.0, and strata=/start=/entry=/robust=/cluster= are pre-existing feature-cluster kwargs -- a grep of drivers/survival confirmed no live renamed spelling, so NO driver edits were needed this cycle. The Powerhouse (Apple Silicon; CPU fp64 + Metal/MPS fp32; R 4.5.2 with survival 3.8.3; Apple Accelerate BLAS) legs were RE-RUN LIVE on 5.0.0 vs R and every number reproduces the 4.8.0 report within the already-tolerated round-off / stochastic / timing tiers, confirming the rename introduced no numeric change: correctness (KM/log-rank/Cox/discrete all machine-precision, coxph concordance EXACT at 1.11e-16), the A1+VA-8 feature cluster (37 agreement rows, worst max_abs 1.82e-11; coefficients/SEs ~1e-15; includes the A8 Breslow-ties row), the R10 hard-cases cluster (36 rows, worst 6.82e-13), Cox scaling (O(n), py/R 0.7-1.1x), convergence diagnostics (6/6 flag-match), R15 default-invocation (5/5 behaviour-match), and the MPS discrete-time legs (float32 accepted across the flchain sweep ~3e-6..6e-5 vs CPU fp64; the R12/R13 no-silent-wrong boundary: 23 safe + 2 refused-force-recovers, NO accepted-but-wrong band; MPS device-pivot scaling). The Forge/CUDA study group (R12/R13 fp32 gate on CUDA, CUDA device pivots, gpu_fp64 exact path) is CARRIED FORWARD byte-unchanged from v4.8.0: no CUDA host was available this cycle and the GPU kernels are byte-identical across the rename. The CPU-side discrete-time TIMING baseline (scaling_discrete_cpu_powerhouse, the expansion breakdown, and the R-choke sweep) is likewise carried forward from v4.8.0: these are illustrative wall-clock studies on the byte-identical _discrete.py / binomial-GLM estimator, and their ~1M-2M-row CPU + R glm sweeps exceed the harness's single-call execution cap while adding no correctness signal (the MPS side of the device pivot was re-run live). Identical float64 inputs to both engines (each design from the central HDF5 store, R17).

studies.title: Convergence diagnostics .converged / .n_iter vs R -- Powerhouse (CPU) (C5)
studies.note: 4.3.3 closes C5 by exposing DiscreteTimeSolution.converged / .n_iter. The new flag is validated against R glm(binomial)'s OWN convergence determination on the identical person-period design (R9/G3). Both .converged AND .n_iter match R bit-for-bit across well-posed, default, separation-extreme, perfectly-separated-covariate, and all-censored designs: the separated covariate reports converged=True at 18 iterations exactly as R (R also converges on separated data at a large finite coefficient -- not a false positive), and the all-censored degenerate design reports converged=False at the 25-iteration cap, matching R. No false-positive convergence claim.

studies.title: Cox PH CPU scaling vs R -- Powerhouse (CPU / fp64) (priority 3: CPU never lags R)
studies.note: Synthetic proportional-hazards DGP. pystatistics Cox PH is O(n log n) (vectorized reverse-cumsum risk sets + a Fenwick-tree concordance), matching R's complexity: the pystatistics/R wall ratio is FLAT at ~1-2.6x across n=250..8000. Re-run fresh at 4.3.3; reproduces v4.2.4/4.3.2.

studies.title: fp32 GPU no-silent-wrong boundary on discrete-time's regime -- Powerhouse (MPS) (R13/R12)
studies.note: RIGOR R13: the regression R12 fp32 gate is re-proven on discrete-time's OWN person-period regime (heavy low-weight interval-dummy block, near-separation, large coefficients, conditioning) plus a real flchain-quarterly anchor, on the MPS gated-CG path. Every accepted float32 fit reached the float64 optimum (deviance to the fp32 tier); refusals are fail-loud true-positives / conservative refusals that force=True recovers (cond >= 2e5); NO accepted-but-wrong band. Per R9/G3 a reference-degeneracy guard excludes designs whose fp64 reference is itself undefined (a uniformly-deep baseline yields zero events) rather than judging fp32 against a meaningless optimum. Re-run fresh LIVE at 5.0.0 on this Powerhouse MPS host vs R; reproduces v4.8.0 within the float32 tier (rename-only release, engine byte-unchanged).

studies.title: fp32 GPU inference-SE no-understatement on discrete-time's regime -- Powerhouse (MPS) (R13/R12)
studies.note: The R12 proof extended to the INFERENCE outputs (the covariate SEs the user reads). On every accepted float32 fit the covariate SEs track the fp64 CPU fit to the Tier-2 contract (rtol <= 1e-2) and no covariate SE is understated -- instability surfaces in the SE exactly as in R. The float32 discrete-time path never returns a covariate that is wrong AND looks precise. Re-run fresh LIVE at 5.0.0 on this Powerhouse MPS host vs R; reproduces v4.8.0 within the float32 tier (rename-only release, engine byte-unchanged).

studies.title: Discrete-time GPU fit scaling -- Powerhouse: CPU (fp64) vs MPS (fp32)
studies.note: GPU value proposition (priority 4: the GPU must EARN its existence by beating the CPU in its regime). Wall-clock of the binomial GLM fit on the person-period design (expansion excluded). The MPS float32 inner solve is a gated matrix-free conjugate gradient (squaring-free); MPS converges across the whole flchain sweep including quarterly and monthly, and wins materially over the CPU at scale. Reproduces v4.2.4 at 4.3.2.

record_fields.max_abs: max absolute difference between pystatistics and R over a quantity's elements
record_fields.max_rel: max relative difference between pystatistics and R over a quantity's elements (correctness headline)
record_fields.n_elements: number of scalar elements compared for that quantity (1 for scalars, vector length otherwise)
record_fields.speedup_vs_r: R wall-clock / pystatistics wall-clock on the same fit (>1 means pystatistics is faster)
record_fields.ratio_pystat_over_r: pystatistics wall-clock / R wall-clock at a given n (flat across n once both are O(n log n))
record_fields.peak_mem_mb: peak memory during the fit (GPU allocator high-water mark; process RSS delta on CPU)
record_fields.coef_max_rel: max relative difference of the float32 GPU covariate coefficients vs the CPU fp64 fit (float32 tier ~1e-5 when accepted)
record_fields.forced_max_rel: RIGOR R9: max relative error of the REJECTED float32 fit if forced (large -> the fit is genuinely wrong -> the rejection is a correct fail-loud)
record_fields.faithfulness_rel: max relative difference between regression.fit on the reconstructed person-period design and the public discrete_time coefficients (~0 -> the fit-isolated measurement is faithful)
record_fields.expansion_frac_of_e2e: person-period expansion time / end-to-end discrete_time time (small at scale -> the GLM fit dominates)
record_fields.cov_coef_max_rel_vs_r: R15: max relative difference of the DEFAULT invocation's covariate coefficients vs R glm on the identical every-unique-event-time design (~1e-15 -> the default matches R)
record_fields.baseline_hazard_max: R15: the largest per-interval baseline hazard under the default binning (reaches 1.0 only in the no-censoring separation extreme, matching R)
record_fields.accepted_dev_rel_vs_fp64: R13/R12: deviance of an ACCEPTED float32 fit vs the fp64 reference (<= fp32 tier -> the right optimum; a large value would be a silent-wrong fit)
record_fields.forced_dev_rel_vs_fp64: R13/R12: deviance of a REFUSED fit when FORCED, vs fp64 (large/non-finite -> the refusal was a correct true-positive)
record_fields.se_rel_gpu_vs_cpu: R13/R12 inference: max relative gap of the accepted float32 covariate SEs vs the fp64 CPU SEs (<= Tier-2 1e-2; never understated)
record_fields.classification: R13/R12 boundary verdict: safe / refused-true-positive / refused-force-recovers / ref-degenerate (excluded) / SILENT-WRONG
record_fields.inference_verdict: R13/R12 inference verdict: inference-warned / refused (fail-loud) / INFERENCE-SILENT-WRONG
record_fields.py_converged: C5: the new DiscreteTimeSolution.converged flag (4.3.3) vs R glm's converged
